proposed.text: An architect signed and sealed architectural drawings prepared by a consulting firm, making only minor modifications to adapt the design to a different site. Later, construction problems occurred because the building was not properly adapted for the site. What is the architect's signing/sealing exposure?

options.text: The architect is not liable because the design was prepared by the consulting firm, which should have ensured site compatibility
The architect is liable; the signature certifies personal responsibility for the document regardless of who prepared it
The architect's liability is limited to the portion of the document the architect personally modified, provided those modifications were substantial
The architect is liable only if the modifications were inadequate to address site-specific concerns, which must be proven by the consulting firm

rationale.a: Signing and sealing the set prevents the architect from treating the consultant's authorship as a complete shield.
rationale.c: Section 20 and Section 32 tie responsibility to architectural documents issued under the architect's seal or authorized signature, not only to visible minor edits.
rationale.d: The checked source does not shift the burden to the consulting firm as the condition for the signing architect's exposure.
rationale.correct: RA 9266 IRR Section 20 and Section 32 tie responsibility to architectural documents issued under the architect's seal or authorized signature. Section 23 adds discipline exposure if the documents were not personally prepared or executed under immediate supervision.
rationale.takeaway: A seal on borrowed drawings carries real responsibility; minor adaptation does not erase Section 23 exposure.

proposed.explanation: Corrected the sealing typo and aligned the exposure to RA 9266 IRR Sections 20, 23, and 32: the seal/signature carries responsibility and Section 23 risk if the work was not personally prepared or immediately supervised.
